requirement: Link students and courses through an association table, enrolling a student at most once per course, refusing enrolment into a course whose seats are all taken, and listing a course's students alphabetically.
skeleton: An enrollments Table with a composite primary key, Student and Course models with secondary relationships using back_populates, enroll checking existence, duplicate membership and course capacity before appending and committing, and roster returning sorted names.
caption: Many-to-many relationships with SQLAlchemy 2.0. The enrollments association Table in Base.metadata has student_id and course_id columns, each a ForeignKey and together the composite primary key, so a pair can exist only once. Student.courses and Course.students are relationship objects with secondary=enrollments and back_populates pointing at each other; Course also has a title and an integer capacity. enroll(session, student_id, course_id) loads both with session.get and raises LookupError saying student N not found or course N not found. If the course is already in the student's courses it returns False before anything else, so re-enrolling in a full course is still a harmless no-op. Otherwise, when the course's own student count has reached its capacity, it raises ValueError saying course TITLE is full; else it appends the course, commits and returns True. roster(session, course_id) returns the course's student names sorted alphabetically and raises LookupError for an unknown course. The fixture asserts the roster order and association row count, that a second enrolment returns False, that the third student in a two-seat course raises ValueError while re-enrolling an existing member returns False, that a student's other courses do not count against a course's capacity, and that unknown ids raise LookupError.

constraints: Students and courses are linked through an association table
Enrolling an already enrolled student returns False
A course cannot hold more students than its capacity; the next one raises ValueError
Capacity counts the course's students, not the student's courses

rationale.teaches: A secondary association Table with a composite primary key and paired back_populates relationships, with idempotency checked before capacity.
rationale.why: Appending an existing link violates the association key only at flush time, and checking capacity first turns a harmless repeat into an error, while counting the wrong side of the relationship passes with a single course.

ops.docstring: Students and courses linked through an association table.

ops.stmt: from sqlalchemy import Column, ForeignKey, String, Table
from sqlalchemy.orm import DeclarativeBase, Mapped, Session, mapped_column, relationship

ops.source:
class Base(DeclarativeBase):
    """Declarative base for this module's tables."""

enrollments = Table(
    "enrollments",
    Base.metadata,
    Column("student_id", ForeignKey("students.id"), primary_key=True),
    Column("course_id", ForeignKey("courses.id"), primary_key=True),
)

class Student(Base):
    """A student taking any number of courses."""

    __tablename__ = "students"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50))
    courses: Mapped[list["Course"]] = relationship(
        secondary=enrollments, back_populates="students"
    )

class Course(Base):
    """A course with a fixed number of seats."""

    __tablename__ = "courses"

    id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(primary_key=True)
    title: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(50))
    capacity: Mapped[int]
    students: Mapped[list[Student]] = relationship(
        secondary=enrollments, back_populates="courses"
    )

candidates.why_wrong: A repeat enrolment appends the link again and fails on the association primary key.
The strict comparison lets one student more than the capacity enrol.
The roster keeps relationship order instead of sorting names alphabetically.
Capacity is checked before membership, so re-enrolling in a full course raises instead of returning False.
Capacity is compared with the student's course count instead of the course's student count.
